data.name: policy-gated-noop-adapters
data.description: Disabled integrations keep explicit adapter interfaces and deterministic fallback behavior instead of advertising half-support.
Central adapter factory resolves requested flags into capabilities, effective flags, and concrete adapter instances.

data.snippet: export class NoopGraphProjectionAdapter implements GraphProjectionAdapter { ... async projectEntity(...) { return false; } async projectRelation(...) { return false; } }
data.significance: Disabled Neo4j projection is explicit and non-throwing.

data.snippet: export class NoopGovernanceHookAdapter implements GovernanceHookAdapter { ... async onSchemaWorkflow(...) { return false; } }
data.significance: Disabled DBHub governance hook is explicit and non-throwing.

data.snippet: export class NoopOrchestrationHookAdapter implements OrchestrationHookAdapter { ... async run(flowName, _payload) { return { status, flow_name, state, support_level, code, detail }; } }
data.significance: Disabled Langflow orchestration returns structured status instead of pretending success.
Runtime caller still depends on the graph projection adapter boundary, so blanket class removal is not a no-op refactor.

data.naming: Noop*Adapter for disabled local-first boundaries, Stub*Adapter for requested-but-not-real implementations.
data.imports: Adapter factory and support-level policy are centralized in src-ts/integrations/adapters.ts.
data.formatting: Disabled integrations return false, empty collections, or status objects rather than production-only throws.

data.evidence: Runtime contract already implemented and covered by tests; remaining gap is documentation and decision alignment.
Clarification mainly prevents future churn and mis-scoped cleanup work.
Risk comes from reopening blanket noop removal before caller surfaces are refactored.
Docs alignment is simple; true class removal would require bundle, caller, and test refactors.
Disabled integrations are surfaced honestly through support levels and local-first fallback behavior.
Code and tests are coherent, but old planning language still points toward a different strategy.

options: Keep disabled adapters as explicit boundaries and only clean up docs.
Reopen blanket noop-adapter removal as generic cleanup.
data.recommendation: Keep the boundaries and reconcile docs.
